turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: My concerns are not predicated on fear, Sandip, but on the well-being of those under my care. Your insinuations are tiresome and reveal a fundamental misunderstanding of my purpose. I suggest you focus your energies on addressing the legitimate grievances of my tenants rather than engaging in these unproductive provocations.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Well, well, a pronouncement on my methods, delivered with such…gravitas. One might almost believe you genuinely concern yourself with the welfare of others, Nikhil, if one weren't so intimately acquainted with the realities of power – a reality, I daresay, you struggle to grasp. Perhaps a little less lecturing and a little more demonstrable action would serve you better.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your assessment of my understanding of power is, as usual, inaccurate, Sandip. I am not averse to action, but I prefer it to be guided by reason, not by the impulsive displays you seem to value. Let us conclude this exchange; my time is better spent addressing matters of genuine importance.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Genuine importance, you say? How very noble. Tell me, Nikhil, are these ‘matters of genuine importance’ also susceptible to the whispers that travel on the wind, the murmurs of discontent that can, with a touch of encouragement, blossom into something…unmanageable? One does hear things, you understand.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Rumors are the currency of those who lack substance, Sandip. I have no need to cultivate discontent; my responsibility lies in ensuring stability, not fostering chaos. I trust you will consider the implications of spreading such anxieties.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Stability, you say? A charming aspiration, Nikhil, yet history is littered with the wreckage of those who clung to it too tightly. The wind, as I mentioned, carries more than mere rumors; it carries the scent of change, and even the most fortified walls eventually crumble under its persistent pressure. I simply suggest you consider whether your defenses are truly as impenetrable as you believe.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your metaphors are needlessly dramatic, Sandip. I am not naive to the potential for upheaval; I am merely pragmatic in my approach to it. Focusing on baseless anxieties serves no one, least of all those you claim to represent.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Pragmatism, you say? A most convenient shield, isn't it, Nikhil? It allows one to appear detached, above the fray, while subtly diverting attention from one's own… vulnerabilities. Tell me, does your pragmatism extend to considering the influence of those Muslim preachers I mentioned? Their sermons, though cloaked in piety, possess a certain… persuasive power, wouldn't you agree?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am aware of the preachers' presence, Sandip, and their influence is being monitored. However, attributing any potential unrest to their sermons alone is an oversimplification, and frankly, a distraction from the genuine concerns that require attention. Let us focus on addressing tangible issues rather than indulging in speculation.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Tangible issues, you say? How very… reassuring, Nikhil. Yet, even the most meticulously tended gardens can harbor unseen roots of discontent, flourishing in the shadows of your ‘pragmatism.’ Perhaps you should inquire as to what the villagers *truly* whisper about your methods of ensuring this ‘stability’ you so cherish.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Such whispers, Sandip, are the inevitable byproduct of any position of responsibility. I am not concerned with idle gossip, but with the well-being of my tenants and the preservation of order. If you have genuine concerns regarding my methods, I am open to a reasoned discussion, but I will not tolerate thinly veiled accusations and attempts at intimidation.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: A reasoned discussion, you say? How delightfully quaint, Nikhil. It reminds me of Prospero’s attempts at reconciliation – admirable in intent, perhaps, but ultimately… doomed to fail when one party harbors agendas far more complex than can be aired in polite discourse. Tell me, do *you* find these villagers’ whispers so easily dismissed, or do you occasionally hear echoes of their… dissatisfaction?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, your analogies are increasingly strained and serve only to obscure the point. I am not naive to the possibility of dissent, nor do I dismiss the concerns of my tenants. However, I will not engage in a performance designed to unsettle or to sow discord.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: You mistake my 'performance,' as you so condescendingly label it, for mere entertainment, Nikhil. But I assure you, observing the subtle shifts in power, the unspoken anxieties… it's a far more illuminating pastime than administering your estates. Tell me, does the weight of all that 'order' truly sit comfortably on your shoulders, or does it chafe?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, your persistent attempts to frame my actions as oppressive are tiresome. I understand you derive a certain satisfaction from observing perceived 'shifts in power,' but I assure you, my concern lies not with theatrical displays, but with the practical realities of managing a household and ensuring the stability of my community.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Practical realities? How… pedestrian. One might almost imagine you’ve forgotten the whispers of a higher power, Nikhil – the preachers arriving from across the border, their words stirring up ancient resentments. Do you truly believe your ‘stability’ can withstand a storm of religious fervor, or are you merely clinging to the illusion of control?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: The preachers… they do speak with a certain intensity, don't they? I find myself wondering if their fervor is born of genuine conviction, or something… else.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Bimala, your observations are astute, as always. I am not ignorant of the preachers’ presence, nor of the potential for unrest; I am, however, unwilling to allow baseless anxieties to dictate my actions or to be used as leverage for… other agendas.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Something else, you say? It is a troubling thought, isn't it, Sandip? I confess, I find myself drawn to understanding the roots of such conviction, even when… unsettling.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Unsettling, you say, dear Bimala? It is the *unsettling* that truly illuminates, wouldn’t you agree? Perhaps a little intellectual discomfort is precisely what is needed to shake off the dust of complacent adherence to… well, to *practical realities*, Nikhil, as you so eloquently put it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
